system_map.overview: The repository contains the CAS Runner, a CLI-driven tool for continuous architecture workflows, alongside a structured knowledge base (cas-knowledge) containing templates, governance, and project data. The codebase follows a layered layout with CLI, runner, governance, and model definitions.

orchestration.description: FlowRunner sits between CLI and lower-level services; it coordinates execution steps and mediates between governance, LLM, and storage.

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Domain entities for governance, health, and skill evaluation are modeled as Pydantic v2 classes, providing validation, serialization, and schema adherence.
patterns.intent: Create type-safe, reusable domain representations that can be persisted and exchanged via JSON/YAML.
patterns.context: The system tracks governance inventory, compliance findings, health metrics, and skill eval results. These need to be validated, serialized, and processed consistently.
patterns.solution: Define dedicated Pydantic models for each domain concept. Use nested models to represent aggregates. Rely on Pydantic's validation and ORM/JSON capabilities.
implementation_signals: Model classes in separate modules per concern

failure_modes: Version drift between models and persisted artifacts

patterns.reuse_notes: Reusable pattern for any domain subsystem requiring robust data transfer and storage.

extraction_metadata.method: Static analysis of module symbols and dependencies

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: Governance actions are constrained by an explicit transition registry that defines allowable state changes.
patterns.intent: Centralize the rules of valid state changes to avoid scattered conditions and improve auditability.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionEngine processes actions that move governance entities between states; illegal transitions should be rejected consistently.
patterns.solution: Create a TransitionRegistry data structure that maps from source state to a set of allowed target states. The GovernanceActionEngine consults this registry before executing any action.

costs: Registry can become a single point of change
failure_modes: Incomplete transition table could block legitimate updates

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any stateful workflow with well-defined states and transitions.

patterns.name: LLM Client Abstraction with Strategy Implementations
patterns.summary: LLM interactions are behind an abstraction, with a real client and a mock client as interchangeable strategies.
patterns.intent: Isolate LLM calls so they can be swapped for testing or provider changes without affecting the rest of the system.
patterns.context: FlowRunner needs LLM capabilities but must also run deterministic local tests and support multiple providers.
patterns.solution: Define a common interface (implied) for LLM clients and provide LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient implementations. Consumers depend on the abstraction, not on concrete providers.
implementation_signals: Separate modules for real and mock clients
Both client classes are used by FlowRunner
Configuration selects which client to instantiate

failure_modes: Interface expectations may diverge between real and mock

patterns.reuse_notes: Common strategy pattern, applicable to any external service integration.

patterns.name: Thin CLI Delegation to FlowRunner
patterns.summary: The CLI is a thin adapter that parses commands and delegates execution to the FlowRunner, avoiding business logic in the entrypoint.
patterns.intent: Separate user-facing concerns from core workflow logic, improving testability and maintainability.
patterns.context: The primary interface is a command-line tool, but underlying workflows are nontrivial and need independent testing.
forces: Core logic should be callable without CLI
patterns.solution: Keep cli.py minimal, with main() responsible for argument parsing and invoking FlowRunner. The FlowRunner contains the execution orchestration logic.
implementation_signals: CLI does not import domain internals directly

benefits: Clean separation of UI and logic
failure_modes: CLI could still become fat if not disciplined

patterns.name: Governance Block Merge Bootstrap
patterns.summary: During workspace initialization, bootstrap merges a centralized CAS governance block into Claude settings and related configuration files.
patterns.intent: Enforce consistency of agent/governance configuration by deriving it from a single source of truth.
patterns.context: The project needs to distribute governance rules across different tool configuration files (e.g., .claude/settings.json) without manual duplication.
patterns.solution: Use bootstrap functions to read a governance block and merge it into target JSON/YAML files, creating symlinks or copies as needed. This ensures the workspace starts in a known state.

failure_modes: Merge logic errors when source format changes

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for monorepo tools that need to inject common settings into multiple config files.

patterns.name: Compliance Engine as Dedicated Validator
patterns.summary: The system isolates compliance checking into a dedicated ComplianceEngine that produces findings, rather than scattering validation logic.
patterns.intent: Keep validation rules centralized and separate from the rest of the business logic.
patterns.context: Architecture decisions need to be validated against governance rules, and results need to be aggregated.
patterns.solution: Create a ComplianceEngine class that accepts inputs and returns structured ComplianceFinding objects. Decouple it from action execution and health calculation.

costs: Potential to become a God object if too many rules
failure_modes: Engine may not scale if it accumulates many checks

patterns.reuse_notes: Pattern for any rule-based validation subsystem.

patterns.name: Health Metric Aggregation
patterns.summary: Dashboard health is computed from underlying metrics via a dedicated calculation function, returning a status and reason list.
patterns.intent: Provide a single, consistent method to derive an overall health status from multiple inputs.
patterns.context: The dashboard needs a concise health indicator based on several numerical and categorical metrics.
patterns.solution: Implement calculate_health to aggregate metrics into a HealthStatus enum, and get_health_reasons to explain the result. Keep this logic in a small module.

benefits: Clear reasons if status is degraded
failure_modes: Status may be too coarse for some viewers

patterns.reuse_notes: Good for any monitoring or dashboard feature.

patterns.name: Governance Action Service Facade
patterns.summary: GovernanceActionService acts as a facade over the GovernanceActionEngine, offering a simplified interface for executing governance actions.
patterns.intent: Simplify interaction with the action engine and isolate its internal complexity from callers.
patterns.context: Callers need to trigger governance actions without knowing details about engine internals, transition registries, or validation.
patterns.solution: Wrap GovernanceActionEngine in GovernanceActionService, exposing domain-friendly methods and managing any necessary orchestration.
implementation_signals: Callers import the service, not the engine

failure_modes: Service may become a god facade if too much responsibility accumulates

patterns.reuse_notes: Facade pattern is useful for exposing a clean API over a complex subsystem.

patterns.name: Skill Evaluation Suite Modeling
patterns.summary: Skills are evaluated using a structured model of suites, cases, assertions, and results, enabling repeatable and comparable assessments.
patterns.intent: Define a formal structure for skill evaluations to support automated testing and reporting.
patterns.context: The project includes skill evaluation workflows that need to assert expected behaviors and capture outcomes.
patterns.solution: Introduce Pydantic models representing evaluation suites, cases, assertions, and results. Use an EvalStatus enum and structured reports.

benefits: Easy to extend with new assert types
Reports can be serialized and stored
failure_modes: Overly strict assertion model could hinder flexibility

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any agent skill or CLI capability testing.

anti_patterns.name: Duplicate Skill Definitions Across .agents and .claude
symptoms: The same skill names (cas-add-or-modify-feature, cas-drawio-generator, etc.) appear both under .agents/skills and .claude/skills.
Any update to one copy may not be reflected in the other.
suggested_remediation: Centralize skill definitions in a common directory and reference from vendor-specific paths
Add symlink or build step to synchronize copies

anti_patterns.name: Unpinned Installer Dependencies in CI Workflows
symptoms: Validation script checks for no_unpinned_installers, suggesting unpinned installers were present or expected.
The script also checks zero_hardcoding, implying hardcoded values are a concern.
impact: Unexpected CI failures when dependency versions change
Security risk from unpinned supply chain
suggested_remediation: Pin all installer dependencies to exact versions

anti_patterns.name: Multiple Top-Level Docs That Can Drift
symptoms: ARCHITECTURE.md, DESIGN.md, REVIEW.md, RUNBOOK.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and others all exist at root.
No clear ownership or generation mechanism for these docs.
suggested_remediation: Designate a single source of truth for architecture documentation
Generate docs from templates or centralize in cas-knowledge

cross_cutting_concerns.description: Bootstrap and governance merge functions ensure configuration is coherent across tool files, but multiple formats (YAML/JSON) require careful handling.
OpenTelemetry dependencies indicate tracing/logging support, but no specific instrumentation points were visible in the provided sources.
Pydantic and jsonschema are used across the system to enforce data shapes, from LLM configuration to governance artifacts.
The knowledge base under cas-knowledge tracks decisions, patterns, and governance, suggesting a need for coherent versioning and migration.
